reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a more balanced approach, prioritizing both endurance building (long runs and aerobic sessions) and targeted speed work (tempo and interval runs). Plan B, while including tempo runs, focuses heavily on threshold work with minimal variation and two consecutive rest days, which could lead to overtraining and reduced recovery. Plan A’s inclusion of strength training and cross-training also addresses crucial aspects of trail running performance – stability, injury prevention, and overall fitness – that are largely absent in Plan B.
